plain.li: Easy now. Easy.
There you go, that's it.
Hold still, you great lump.
[job:milk] Steady, girl, nearly done.
[job:milk] Don't you dare kick that bucket.
[job:milk] My hands are warm, I promise.
[job:shear] You'll feel lighter, I swear it.
[job:shear] Stop wriggling or you'll get a haircut you'll regret.
[job:shear,summer] There. Cooler already, aren't you?
[job:tame] I won't hurt you, look, I've got food.
[job:tame] Come on. Just a little closer.
[job:tame,wild] I know, I'd be wary of me too.
[job:train] Once more, from the top.
[job:train] Sit. No. Sit!
[job:train,named] Look at me, {PET_nameDef}, not at my pocket.
[job:tend] This will sting, sorry.
[job:tend] Brave thing. Nearly done.
[job:feed] Slowly. It isn't going anywhere.
[job:rescue] Up you come. I've got you.
[job:rope] Come on, this way, home.
[job:rope] No, the pen's the other way.
[childplay] Do you want to be my friend?
[childplay] Stay still, I'm going to pat you very gently.
[childplay] I'll tell you a secret about the cook, but you can't tell.
[childplay,young] You're only little, like me.
[bonded,named] You're my best friend, {PET_nameDef}, but don't tell the others.
[bonded] I'm here. I'm always here.
[young] You'll grow into those legs one day.
[oldanimal] No hurry, old friend, take your time.
[oldanimal,named] Still the best of them, aren't you, {PET_nameDef}?
[pokemon] Ready? Good. Let's work on that move again.
[pokemon] Back in the ball after this, then berries.
[pokemon,job:tend] No potion, sorry, you'll have to make do with me.
[winter] Sorry, my hands are freezing.
[rain] I know, I'm wet too, nearly done.
[night] Shh, the others are asleep.

warm.li: Good animal. You're such a good animal.
[bonded] You're the best of the lot, you know that.

cheerful.li: [job:shear] Look at you. All fluffy, and then not!

gloomy.li: At least you don't complain about the food.
[oldanimal] We're both getting old, you and me.

plain.li: Come on then, {PET_nameDef}, you can help.
Where I go, you go, is that it?
Keep up, then, {PET_nameDef}.
You're underfoot again, not that I mind.
[night] Bedtime for both of us, {PET_nameDef}?
[rain] You'll get soaked following me about.
[pokemon] Out of the ball and straight to my heels, good.
[working] I've got work to do, but you can watch.

warm.li: There you are, I wondered where you'd got to.

gloomy.li: At least somebody wants my company.

plain.li: There. That's the best sound in the colony.
They're all here, every one.
I'll just sit and watch them eat a while.
[child] I'm naming that one, it's mine now.
[evening] They're settling down for the night, look.
[spring] Fresh grass, and they know it.
[winter] All huddled up together, sensible things.

warm.li: Hello, all of you, have you had a good day?

cheerful.li: Best seats in the colony, right here.

gloomy.li: They don't worry about a thing, lucky beasts.

cold.li: All accounted for, coats in order.

plain.li: Stand still and I'll get the burrs out.
Rolled in something again, did you?
[named] Hold still, {OTHER_nameDef}, nearly there.
[bonded] Let's get you shining, my favorite.
[winter] Good thick coat this year, you'll need it.
[summer] You're shedding all over me.

warm.li: You like it behind the ears, don't you?

cheerful.li: Who's going to be the handsomest animal in the colony?

gloomy.li: Somebody has to look after you properly, so it'll be me.

cold.li: Grooming keeps the skin healthy, so hold still.

plain.li: [named] Welcome to the herd, {PET_nameDef}.
[named] You look like a {PET_nameDef}, so that's your name.
[named] You've a name now, {PET_nameDef}, so stay close to your mother.
[nonamed] Hello, little one, welcome.
[nonamed] There you are, and all in one piece.

cheerful.li: [named] Best name I've thought of all year, {PET_nameDef}!

cold.li: [named] You'll do, {PET_nameDef}, you look healthy enough.

plain.li: [named] A young {KIND} born to {OTHER_nameDef}. I went down and named it {PET_nameDef} before anyone else could.
[named] New in the herd: {PET_nameDef}, all legs. Its mother, {OTHER_nameDef}, wouldn't let me near at first.
[nonamed] A young one born to {OTHER_nameDef}, already named by someone quicker than me.
[winter,named] Born in the cold, {PET_nameDef}. I put extra straw down and stayed until it was feeding.

warm.li: [named] {PET_nameDef}, the newest of us. I sat a long while just watching it breathe.

cheerful.li: [named] Welcome, {PET_nameDef}. The herd keeps growing and I keep running out of names!

cold.li: [named] One birth in the herd, a young {KIND}, named {PET_nameDef}. Mother and young both well.

plain.li: [sick] {PAWN_nameDef}, the herdmaster, told {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} was resting and taking water.
[sick] {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} what {PET_nameDef}'s illness was and what to watch for.
[hurt] {PAWN_nameDef} came by to tell {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef}'s wound was clean and closing.
[hurt] {PAWN_nameDef} showed {OTHER_nameDef} how to change {PET_nameDef}'s dressing, and stayed while {OTHER_pronoun} tried.
{PAWN_nameDef} talked {OTHER_nameDef} through {PET_nameDef}'s care, step by step.

warm.li: {PAWN_nameDef} saw how worried {OTHER_nameDef} was about {PET_nameDef} and stayed to talk until {OTHER_pronoun} was calmer.

blunt.li: {PAWN_nameDef} told {OTHER_nameDef} that {PET_nameDef} would live, and to go and get some sleep.

cold.li: {PAWN_nameDef} gave {OTHER_nameDef} a plain account of {PET_nameDef}'s condition, without softening any of it.

plain.li: [first] A year ago today the first young {SUBJECT} was born to the colony's herd. {A_nameDef} remembers how long it took to stand, and wants the day marked.
[years] {YEARS} years now since the herd's first young {SUBJECT}. {A_nameDef} still tells the story of that birth to anyone who'll listen.
The first foal's day. {A_nameDef} has been out with the animals since first light, brushing every one of them.
[tradition] The first foal's day comes round again. As every year, the herd gets an extra measure of feed before anyone else eats.
[spring] The first foal's day, in the season of births. {A_nameDef} has been round the herd counting swollen bellies.

cheerful.li: It's the first foal's day! {A_nameDef} has been round the herd with treats in both pockets.

cold.li: The anniversary of the herd's first birth. {A_nameDef} has noted the date, and the size of the herd then and now.

plain.li: [new] Our herd's first young one, a {SUBJECT}. I keep going back to look at it.
[new] Born here, to animals we raised ourselves. I can't stop grinning about it.
[!new,first] A year since our first foal. I went to look at the herd and couldn't tell which one it was any more.
[!new,years] {YEARS} years since the first foal. I went out to the animals at dawn, as I do on this day.
[!new,tradition] The first foal's day, kept as always. The herd got its extra feed before we got ours.

warm.li: [new] Our first foal. I could watch it for hours, and nearly did.

cheerful.li: [new] Our first baby animal. I want to name it everything!

gloomy.li: [new] A new life in the herd. I hope this place is kinder to it than it's been to us.

cold.li: [new] The herd has bred for the first time. The colony's food supply is more secure for it.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} how long the first foal took to stand.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} tried to work out which of the herd came from the first foal.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} what {B_pronoun} remembered of the day the first foal was born.
[first] A year ago today {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} has hardly said a word since breakfast.
[years] It's {YEARS} years since {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} still keeps the old collar on a nail by the bed.
{DEAD}'s day. {A_nameDef} saved the best scraps from last night's supper and set them out where {DEAD} used to sleep.
[tradition] Every year on this day the colony remembers {DEAD}, the best {SUBJECT} there ever was, and {A_nameDef} tells the story of how they met.
[winter] It was cold like this the day {DEAD} died. {A_nameDef} sat out in it a long while anyway.

warm.li: It's {DEAD}'s day. {A_nameDef} has been telling anyone who never knew {DEAD} what kind of {SUBJECT} {DEAD} was.

blunt.li: {A_nameDef} went for a walk alone on {DEAD}'s day and came back without a word.

plain.li: [first] A year since {DEAD} died. I still look down for {DEAD} at the door.
[years] {YEARS} years without {DEAD}. Some days it feels like a lot longer, some days like last week.
{DEAD}'s day. I sat where {DEAD} used to sleep and told {DEAD} about the year. Silly, I know.
[tradition] {DEAD}'s day, kept as always. The others let me tell the old stories again.

warm.li: I'm grateful for every year I had with {DEAD}. I wish there'd been more.

cheerful.li: {DEAD}'s day. I've been telling the old {DEAD} stories, and the others still laugh in the right places.

gloomy.li: Nothing has been quite as good since {DEAD}.

cold.li: {DEAD}'s day. I marked it. I find I still miss {DEAD} more than I expected.

plain.li: {A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} about {DEAD}, and the time {DEAD} stole a whole ham off the table.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} where {DEAD} used to like to sleep.
{A_nameDef} asked {B_nameDef} what {B_pronoun} remembered of {DEAD}.
